'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2022 Taiwanese local elections]]
**Residents of [[Taiwan]] head to the polls to elect mayors, city council members and other local leaders in nine cities and 13 counties. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-63739622 (BBC News)]
**The [[Kuomintang|Kuomintang Party]], who has consistently advocated economic engagement and unification with [[China|mainland China]], wins 13 of the 21 seats contested in the elections. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-63768538 (CNN)]
**[[President of the Republic of China|Taiwanese President]] [[Tsai Ing-wen]] resigns as [[List of leaders of the Democratic Progressive Party|leader of the Democratic Progressive Party]] after the party suffers a major defeat in the elections. [https://apnews.com/article/taiwan-china-5961a55b01706318c3187ed292f70d0f (AP)]
*[[2022 Taiwanese constitutional referendum]]
**Residents of [[Taiwan]] head to the polls for a [[constitutional referendum]] on the issues of lowering the [[voting age]] from 20 to 18 and lowering the [[age of candidacy]] from 23 to 18. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-63739622 (BBC News)]
**The propositions on lowering voting and candidacy ages to 18 fail to pass as they do not receive the required approval of half of the eligible voters. [https://focustaiwan.tw/politics/202211260030 (Focus Taiwan)] 
*[[2022 Equatorial Guinean general election]]
**[[President of Equatorial Guinea|President]] [[Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo]], the world's [[List of current state leaders by date of assumption of office|longest-serving president]], is re-elected to a seven-year term. [https://www.barrons.com/news/obiang-re-elected-as-e-guinea-ruler-with-94-9-of-vote-01669488906 (AFP via ''Barron's'')]
*[[2017–present Peruvian political crisis]]
**[[Betssy Chávez]] is sworn in as the new [[Prime Minister of Peru]] after [[Aníbal Torres]]' resignation. [https://www.msn.com/en-xl/news/other/pedro-castillo-swears-in-betssy-chávez-as-peru-s-new-prime-minister/ar-AA14z0GD (MSN)]
